chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive in the land spreading corruption is only that they be killed or crucified"

To the end of the verse. So I said: Which of these prescribed punishments that Allah has named applies to them? He said: "That is up to the Imam: if he wills, he amputates; if he wills, he crucifies; if he wills, he banishes; and if he wills, he kills." I said: Banishment to where? He said: "He is banished from one town to another town."
And he said: "Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام banished two men from al-Kūfah to al-Baṣrah."

key_terms.فَسَادًا: corruption and violent disorder spread in the land
key_terms.مِصْرٍ: a town or city to which or from which exile takes place
key_terms.نَفَى: banished or exiled from one place
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ: wage war or hostile opposition in the legal sense mentioned in the verse
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the divinely authorized leader who determines the applicable punishment
key_terms.ٱلْحُدُودِ: the prescribed penal punishments named by Allah

ai.seo_question: Who decides which punishment applies in the verse about those who wage war against Allah and spread corruption in the land?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse concerning those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread فساد in the land. It states that determining which punishment is to be applied is delegated to the Imam, and it clarifies that banishment means being removed from one town to another. The report also cites a precedent from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام.
